name: Pixel grid
summary: A picture or a letter built from square cells that are each on or off, or one flat colour, with no curve and no smooth edge.
how: Draw an icon on a grid of 16 or 32 cells a side; fill each cell with one colour or leave it empty.
Limit the palette to 1 to 16 colours; do not blend two colours inside one cell.
Draw a diagonal as a stair of equal steps, for example 2 cells across for each 1 cell up.
Show the image at an integer scale (2x, 3x, 4x) so that no cell blurs.

origin.note: Ken Knowlton writes BEFLIX, a language that draws computer films as grids of cells in a small set of grey tones.

adoptions.via: The Xerox Alto has a bitmap display, and its programs draw icons cell by cell.
Susan Kare draws the Macintosh icons and the Chicago bitmap face on a grid of 32 by 32 cells.
Zuzana Licko draws the Emigre bitmap faces for the 72 dpi screen and the dot-matrix printer.
The eBoy group publishes pixel illustrations of cities and objects on the web.
Japanese portal pages set text at 10 to 12 px in bitmap kanji fonts, so each glyph sits on the pixel grid.

sources.title: Susan Kare, Mac icon and font work (Apple Macintosh, 1984)
